breakfast.name: Chipa (Cheese Bread)
instructions: Mix cassava starch with cheese, eggs, milk, butter, anise
Shape into small rolls or rings
Bake at 200°C 20 min until golden
breakfast.description: Chewy cheese bread — Paraguay's national snack, eaten morning to night.

breakfast.name: Cocido (Burned Mate Tea)
instructions: Burn sugar in pot until caramelized
Add yerba mate and water
Boil 3 min, strain
Add hot milk
breakfast.description: Caramelized mate tea with milk — a Paraguayan morning ritual.

breakfast.name: Cocido Quemado (Burnt Mate Tea with Milk)
instructions: Cocido quemado is Paraguay unique breakfast drink -- burnt mate
Unlike Argentine mate (drunk bitter from a gourd), Paraguayan cocido is COOKED on the stove
The technique: put yerba mate and sugar in a pot, heat until sugar caramelizes and burns slightly
Add water and milk -- simmer briefly -- strain into a cup
The result: a tea-like drink with a distinctive burnt-caramel, smoky flavor
This is NOT how any other country drinks mate -- uniquely Paraguayan
Cocido is breakfast -- drunk with chipa or bread
Paraguayan children grow up on cocido -- the first warm drink many learn to love
breakfast.description: Paraguay unique morning drink -- yerba mate and sugar heated together until the sugar caramelizes and burns slightly, then simmered with milk and water. Unlike Argentine bitter mate from a gourd, Paraguayan cocido is cooked on the stove with burnt caramel. A bittersweet, smoky flavor no other country replicates.

breakfast.name: Mbeju (Cheese and Starch Flatbread)
ingredients: Almidon de mandioca (cassava starch -- the key ingredient)
Paraguayan cheese (queso Paraguay -- fresh, salty, crumbly)
instructions: Mbeju is one of Paraguay most beloved traditional foods -- Guarani origin
The name is Guarani -- Paraguay is officially bilingual (Spanish and Guarani)
Most Paraguayan food has Guarani names -- the language IS the cuisine
Almidon de mandioca (cassava starch) is the base -- creates unique chewy-crispy texture
Mix cassava starch with grated queso Paraguay, egg, milk, and butter
Cook on a flat pan -- the mixture spreads and sets into a golden, lacy disc
Texture: crispy on the outside, chewy and stretchy from the cheese inside
Mbeju is breakfast and merienda (afternoon snack) -- versatile across the day
Queso Paraguay (fresh, salty, crumbly) is essential -- no substitution captures it
breakfast.description: Paraguay Guarani-origin flatbread -- cassava starch mixed with queso Paraguay (fresh, salty, crumbly), egg, and butter, cooked into a golden lacy disc that is crispy outside and chewy-stretchy inside. The Guarani language IS the cuisine -- most Paraguayan food has Guarani names. Pre-colonial technique adapted with Spanish dairy.

lunch.name: Sopa Paraguaya (Corn Cake)
instructions: Sauté onions in butter
Mix all ingredients into thick batter
Pour into greased pan
Bake at 180°C 45 min
lunch.description: Paraguay's 'soup' that's actually a savory cornbread — the national dish.

lunch.name: Bori-Bori (Corn Dumpling Soup)
instructions: Make chicken broth with vegetables
Mix corn flour with cheese, shape into small dumplings
Add dumplings to broth
Cook until they float
lunch.description: Chicken soup with cheesy corn dumplings.

lunch.name: Bori Bori (Corn Ball Soup)
ingredients: Corn flour and Paraguayan cheese (for the bori bori balls)
instructions: Bori bori is Paraguay national soup -- chicken broth with corn-and-cheese dumplings
The bori bori: small balls made from corn flour mixed with grated Paraguayan cheese
The balls are dropped into simmering chicken broth -- they cook and float
The corn-cheese combination is the Paraguayan DNA: corn (Guarani) + cheese (Spanish)
Broth is rich with chicken, carrots, squash -- a complete, sustaining soup
Bori bori is winter food -- July-August (winter in the Southern Hemisphere)
The corn balls should be slightly chewy -- the cheese melts inside them
Comfort food -- what Paraguayan mothers make when the family needs warming
lunch.description: Paraguay national soup -- rich chicken broth with bori bori (corn flour and Paraguayan cheese dumplings) that cook and float in the simmering liquid, with carrots and squash. The corn-cheese balls are the Guarani-Spanish fusion DNA: corn (Indigenous) + cheese (colonial). Winter comfort food (July-August).

lunch.name: Soyo (Meat and Vegetable Soup)
ingredients: Ground beef (or minced beef -- pounded in a mortar)
instructions: Soyo is a hearty meat soup -- the everyday Paraguayan lunch
The beef is traditionally pounded in a mortar (tacu) -- not ground by machine
Saute onion, tomato, pepper -- add the pounded meat
Add beef stock, corn kernels, rice or pasta -- simmer until cooked
Soyo is the working person lunch -- cheap, filling, fast
Less famous than bori bori but more commonly eaten everyday
Represents practical Paraguayan cooking -- substance over spectacle
lunch.description: Paraguay everyday lunch -- hearty soup of pounded beef (traditionally in a tacu/mortar), onion, tomato, fresh corn kernels, and rice. The working person lunch: cheap, filling, fast. Less famous than bori bori but more commonly eaten daily.

lunch.name: Milanesa Napolitana
instructions: Milanesa napolitana is popular across the Southern Cone -- Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay
Breaded, fried beef cutlet topped with tomato sauce, ham, and melted mozzarella
Paraguay adopted this from Argentine culinary influence -- shared deep cultural ties
Pound beef thin, bread (flour, egg, breadcrumbs), fry until golden
Top with tomato sauce, ham, mozzarella -- melt under a broiler
Served with fries or rice -- the complete comfort meal
lunch.description: Southern Cone comfort -- breaded fried beef cutlet topped with tomato sauce, ham, and melted mozzarella. Adopted from Argentine culinary influence. Served with fries or rice. Every restaurant in Asuncion serves it.

dinner.name: Asado (BBQ)
instructions: Start wood fire, let coals form
Salt meats generously
Grill slowly over coals
Serve with boiled mandioca
dinner.description: Paraguayan asado — slow-grilled meats over wood coals.

dinner.name: Mbejú (Cassava Starch Cake)
instructions: Mix cassava starch with cheese, egg, butter
Cook on griddle until golden on both sides
Chewy and crispy at the same time
dinner.description: Crispy-chewy cassava starch and cheese flatbread.

dinner.name: Asado Paraguayo (Paraguayan Barbecue)
instructions: Asado is the social ritual of Paraguay -- shared with Argentina, Uruguay, Brazil
The Paraguayan distinction: mandioca (boiled cassava) replaces bread as the starch
Costilla (beef ribs) is the classic Paraguayan asado cut -- low and slow over charcoal
The asado is a social event lasting hours
The asador (grill master) tends the fire -- position of pride and skill
Paraguayan chorizo is fresh (not cured) -- grilled alongside the beef
Salt only -- no marinades, no sauces -- meat quality speaks for itself
Sunday asado is a family institution -- weekly gathering around the grill
The parrilla (grill) is in every Paraguayan backyard -- even modest homes have one
dinner.description: Paraguay social ritual -- beef ribs (costilla) slow-grilled over charcoal, served with boiled mandioca (cassava replaces bread -- the Paraguayan distinction from Argentine asado). Sunday asado is a family institution: hours around the grill, the asador tending fire with pride. Salt only. Every backyard has a parrilla.

dinner.name: Puchero (Boiled Dinner)
ingredients: Vegetables: squash, corn, carrots, cabbage, sweet potato
instructions: Puchero is the South American boiled dinner -- Spanish olla podrida adapted
All the meats boil together: beef, chorizo, morcilla -- the broth becomes rich
Vegetables added by cooking time: root vegetables first, leafy greens last
Mandioca replaces potato in the Paraguayan version -- the local starch
Broth served first as soup -- then meats and vegetables as second course
Puchero is winter food -- heavy, warming, sustaining
The communal pot: everyone eats from the same abundant platter
Puchero feeds a crowd -- scaled up easily for large families
dinner.description: Paraguay communal winter pot -- beef, chorizo, and morcilla boiled together with squash, corn, carrots, and mandioca (cassava replaces potato). Broth served first as soup, then meats and vegetables as second course. Spanish olla podrida adapted. Feeds a crowd easily.

dinner.name: Surubi a la Parrilla (Grilled Catfish)
ingredients: Surubi (striped catfish -- from the Paraguay and Parana Rivers)
instructions: Surubi is Paraguay prized river fish -- the giant catfish of the Paraguay and Parana Rivers
These massive catfish can weigh 50+ kg -- trophy fish of South American rivers
The flesh is firm, white, mild -- excellent for grilling
Marinate briefly in lemon juice, garlic, oil -- grill over charcoal
The firm flesh holds up perfectly on the grill
Served with boiled mandioca and salad -- the river-fish equivalent of asado
Paraguay is landlocked -- the rivers are the source of fish
The Paraguay River is the lifeline -- commerce, food, identity
Asuncion costanera (riverfront) restaurants specialize in surubi
dinner.description: Paraguay river king -- surubi (giant striped catfish from the Paraguay and Parana Rivers, can weigh 50+ kg) grilled over charcoal, served with boiled mandioca and salad. Paraguay is landlocked -- the rivers are the lifeline. Asuncion costanera (riverfront) restaurants specialize in surubi.

snacks.name: Empanadas Paraguayas
ingredients: Filling: ground beef, onion, egg, pepper
instructions: Make dough, cut circles
Fill with beef mixture
Fold, seal with fork
Fry until golden

snacks.name: Empanada Paraguaya
ingredients: Filling: ground beef, onion, bell pepper, hard-boiled egg
Oil for frying or egg wash for baking
instructions: Paraguayan empanadas are typically smaller and simpler than Argentine versions
The filling: ground beef with onion, pepper, and a piece of hard-boiled egg
Can be fried (street food) or baked (home cooking)
Served as merienda (afternoon snack) or appetizer before asado
Found at every market, bus terminal, and street vendor in Asuncion
Paraguayan empanadas are practical food -- eaten on the go, one-handed
snacks.description: Paraguay practical turnover -- smaller and sturdier than Argentine empanadas, filled with ground beef, onion, bell pepper, and a surprise piece of hard-boiled egg. Fried for street food, baked for home. Found at every market and bus terminal in Asuncion.

snacks.name: Pastel Mandio (Cassava Empanada)
ingredients: Filling: ground beef, onion, garlic, cumin
instructions: Pastel mandio uses mandioca (cassava) dough instead of wheat flour -- distinctly Paraguayan
Mandio is the Guarani word for mandioca/cassava -- the language names the food
Boil and mash mandioca until smooth -- form into a dough
Fill with seasoned ground beef, seal into half-moons
Deep-fry until golden -- the cassava crust is crispy and slightly chewy
More authentically Paraguayan than wheat-flour empanadas
snacks.description: Paraguay authentically Guarani turnover -- cassava (mandio in Guarani) boiled, mashed, and shaped around seasoned beef, deep-fried until golden and chewy-crispy. Guarani ingredient + Spanish technique = Paraguayan fusion.

snacks.name: Sopa Paraguaya (Cornbread -- Not Soup)
instructions: Sopa paraguaya is NOT a soup despite the name -- it is a savory cornbread
The name paradox: sopa means soup, but this is a solid, baked corn cake
Legend: a cook tried to make corn soup, added too much corn flour, baked the mistake
Mix corn flour with abundant cheese, sauteed onions, eggs, milk, fat
Pour into a greased baking dish -- bake until golden and set
Texture: dense, moist, intensely cheesy, with sweet caramelized onion
The onion quantity is GENEROUS -- sopa paraguaya should be onion-heavy
Paraguay most iconic food -- alongside chipa
Served alongside asado, at celebrations, at every significant gathering
June 24 (San Juan) is sopa paraguaya biggest day -- the national festival
The only soup you can eat with a fork -- the Paraguayan joke
snacks.description: Paraguay most iconic paradox -- called sopa (soup) but it is a dense, cheesy cornbread. Legend: a cook added too much corn flour to soup, baked the mistake, and sopa paraguaya was born. Corn flour, abundant queso Paraguay, generous sauteed onions, eggs, and fat baked golden. The only soup you eat with a fork.

desserts.name: Dulce de Mamón (Candied Papaya)
instructions: Peel and seed green papaya
Make sugar syrup with spices
Simmer papaya in syrup until translucent
Cool in syrup
desserts.description: Green papaya candied in spiced syrup.

desserts.name: Dulce de Mamon (Candied Green Papaya)
ingredients: Green papaya (unripe -- peeled, cut into chunks)
instructions: Dulce de mamon is Paraguay traditional preserve -- candied green papaya
Mamon is the Paraguayan word for papaya -- green (unripe) papaya is used
Cook in heavy sugar syrup with cloves and cinnamon -- low and slow
The papaya absorbs the syrup -- becoming translucent, sweet, and candy-like
Served as dessert with cheese -- the sweet-salty combination
Every Paraguayan grandmother makes dulce de mamon -- generational knowledge
Spanish colonial spicing (clove-cinnamon) on Indigenous fruit
desserts.description: Paraguay grandmother dessert -- green (unripe) papaya slow-cooked in heavy sugar syrup with cloves and cinnamon until translucent and candy-sweet. Served with cheese (sweet-salty combination). Generational knowledge. Spanish colonial spicing on Indigenous fruit.

desserts.name: Kai Ladrillo (Peanut Brick)
ingredients: Molasses or dark cane syrup (miel de cana)
instructions: Kai ladrillo means monkey brick in Guarani -- a dense peanut-sugar candy
Melt sugar and molasses together -- cook until hard crack stage
Mix in roasted peanuts -- pour onto surface to set into a flat, hard slab
Break into irregular pieces -- the bricks
Extremely hard -- cracked with teeth
The molasses gives a deep, dark sweetness -- not refined-sugar sweet
Countryside candy -- rural Paraguay sweet, made from local peanuts and cane
Sold alongside sopa paraguaya at San Juan festival (June 24)
desserts.description: Paraguay monkey brick -- roasted peanuts set in hard-crack molasses candy, broken into irregular pieces. Guarani-Spanish name: kai (monkey) + ladrillo (brick). Extremely hard, cracked with teeth. Rural countryside candy from local peanuts and sugarcane.

drinks.name: Tereré (Cold Yerba Mate)
instructions: Fill mate cup with yerba
Add cold water and ice
Sip through bombilla straw
Refill repeatedly
drinks.description: Ice-cold mate — Paraguay's national drink, drunk all day long.

drinks.name: Carrulim
instructions: Infuse caña with rue and lemon
Serve as shots
Traditionally drunk on August 1st to ward off evil
drinks.description: Herbal sugarcane spirit drunk ritually on August 1st.

drinks.name: Terere (Cold Mate)
ingredients: Herbs: mint (menta), lemongrass (cedron), or medicinal herbs (yuyos)
Guampa (cow horn cup) and bombilla (metal straw)
instructions: Terere is Paraguay national drink -- UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2020)
It is mate drunk COLD -- ice water instead of hot water
Terere is NOT just cold mate -- distinct practice with different yerba, different ritual
The guampa (horn cup) is filled with yerba mate, then ice-cold water poured from a jug
Medicinal herbs (yuyos) are added to the water: mint, lemongrass, or remedial plants
The yuyos tradition: specific herbs for specific ailments -- folk medicine in the drink
Terere is SOCIAL -- the guampa is passed around the circle, everyone drinks from same bombilla
Refusing terere when offered is rude -- a social contract
In Paraguay brutal summer heat (40C+), terere is survival -- not just refreshment
Paraguayans drink terere all day -- at work, on breaks, while socializing
Terere separates Paraguay from Argentina (hot mate) and Brazil (chimarrao)
drinks.description: Paraguay UNESCO-honored national drink (2020) -- yerba mate drunk ICE-COLD from a guampa (horn cup) through a bombilla (metal straw), with medicinal herbs (yuyos: mint, lemongrass, folk remedies) in the water. Social ritual: the guampa circulates, refusing is rude. In 40C+ heat, terere is survival. Separates Paraguay from Argentina (hot mate).
